item.title: CVE-2026-116225 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.7 | Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the BER decoder in Erlang/OTP snmp allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust CPU via an SNMP message that contains an OBJECT IDENTIFIER with a very long sub-identifier.
snmp_pdus:dec_oid_element/3 does not limit the number of base-128 octets in a sub-identifier, and snmp_pdus:dec_oid_elements/3 does not limit the number of sub-identifiers, so one sub-identifier can span the whole datagram. When the value exceeds the native integer size, each further octet copies a growing bignum, and decoding time grows quadratically with the sub-identifier length. The agent and the manager decode OIDs before they check community strings or SNMPv3 credentials, inside the single network interface process (snmpa_net_if or snmpm_net_if). That process does not read the next datagram until decoding completes.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to snmp from 4.25.1 before 5.18.2.3, 5.20.2.4, and 5.20.7. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to snmp before 4.25.1, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-116293 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.0
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.0 | Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a NEWER_REFERENCE_EXT term with a zero-length ID. decoded_size in erts/emulator/beam/external.c accepts a reference whose 16-bit Len field is zero, but dec_term always reads one ID word. dec_term then runs 4 bytes ahead of the position that decoded_size validated. It decodes the bytes that follow as terms that were never sized, and writes past the reserved process heap.
The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. NEW_REFERENCE_EXT also accepts a zero length, but its range check on the first ID word rejects the shifted input. On 32-bit builds, a zero-length reference of either type at the end of the input, followed by trailing bytes, can write one word past the reserved heap.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-116295 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1 | Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers ('HTTP Request/Response Splitting') vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpc module) allows HTTP Request Splitting.
httpc writes request header names and values to the wire without neutralizing CR, LF or NUL characters. On the default path http_request:mk_key_value_str/2, and with the headers_as_is option httpc_request:http_headers/2, build each header line by plain concatenation of the name, ": ", the value and CRLF. A CR/LF in a name or value ends the header line early. An attacker who controls data that an application puts into a header passed to httpc:request/4,5 can add or override request headers, or append a second request on the same connection.
Applications that pass only constant or validated header names and values are not affected. The request line is not affected, because uri_string rejects URLs that contain raw CR/LF.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-116382 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.2 | Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Erlang OTP inets (httpd_script_env module) allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust the atom table of an httpd server that serves ESI scripts.
When mod_esi builds the environment for an ESI callback, httpd_script_env:http_env_element/3 checks that a request header name already exists as an atom, then creates the atom http_<header-name> with list_to_atom/1. Atoms are never garbage collected, and each new atom passes the existence check on a later request. So a header named node creates http_node, a header named http_node creates http_http_node, and so on. A stream of requests to any ESI URL grows the atom table until it reaches its limit (+t), and then the whole Erlang VM aborts, together with every application on the node.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to inets from 5.10 before 9.3.2.9, 9.6.2.5, and 9.8.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to inets before 5.10, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-117642 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Uncontrolled Recursion vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to abort the Erlang VM via a fun term with funs nested in its integer fields. dec_term in erts/emulator/beam/external.c decodes terms iteratively, except for the OldIndex and OldUniq fields of NEW_FUN_EXT and the Arity field of EXPORT_EXT. For these fields it calls itself, and it checks that the result is a small integer only after the call returns. An input that places another fun in such a field, nested to sufficient depth, recurses once per level, exhausts the stack of the scheduler thread and crashes the VM. The input must be large enough to reach that depth.
The abort takes down every process on the node. Supervision, try/catch and the safe option do not prevent it. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-119443 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in xmerl_scan in Erlang OTP xmerl allows an attacker to exhaust the memory of the Erlang VM via an XML document that names an external DTD.
With default options, xmerl_scan:string/1,2 and xmerl_scan:file/1,2 fetch and parse the external DTD named in a <!DOCTYPE root SYSTEM "..."> declaration. fetch_DTD/2 in lib/xmerl/src/xmerl_scan.erl passes every system identifier to the default fetch function, which maps file: and absolute URIs to local paths, and int_file_decl/3 then reads the whole file with file:read_file/1. This happens whether or not validation is enabled, and the allow_entities option, which is false by default since OTP 27, only governs <!ENTITY> declarations and does not stop the fetch. A document naming file:///dev/zero makes the node read without bound until the operating system kills it for lack of memory, and the parse never returns.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to xmerl from 1.3.7 before 2.1.3.4, 2.1.9.1, and 2.2.1. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to xmerl before 1.3.7, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-120961 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability in the external term format decoder in Erlang OTP erts allows an attacker who controls the input to binary_to_term/1,2 to read memory after the input, and to change one byte there, via a FLOAT_EXT term without a terminating zero byte. decoded_size in erts/emulator/beam/external.c checks only that the 31 bytes of the FLOAT_EXT field are present. dec_term then passes the field to sys_chars_to_double, which scans to a NUL byte without a length limit. When the field has no NUL, the scan continues into the bytes after the field, and those bytes change the decoded float. When the radix character is found after the field and strtod does not accept it, sys_chars_to_double overwrites that byte (a , becomes a .). The VM can fault if the scan reaches an unmapped page.
The safe option does not prevent this. enif_binary_to_term() and the distribution protocol reach the same decoder, and distribution is assumed to run on trusted networks only. The write is limited to the one radix byte. No arbitrary write or code execution was shown.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.20, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.1.3, corresponding to erts from 6.0 before 15.2.7.15, 16.4.0.8, and 17.1.2. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to erts before 6.0, is affected is unknown.

item.title: CVE-2026-124286 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.1 | Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Erlang OTP ssl (ssl_handshake module) allows an on-path attacker to impersonate any server to a TLS 1.2 or DTLS client.
When a server sends no Certificate message and a ServerKeyExchange without a signature, ssl_handshake:decode_server_key/3 reports the signature algorithm as anon, and ssl_handshake:verify_signature/5 returns true for anon without a public key. The client does not require a certificate for a certificate-authenticated key exchange, so the handshake completes for the ecdhe_rsa, ecdhe_ecdsa, dhe_rsa and dhe_dss key exchanges with a cipher suite the client offered. Certificate path validation, verify_fun and the hostname check do not run, and ssl:connect/3 returns {ok, Socket} with {verify, verify_peer} set. The TLS 1.3 client is not affected.
This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.14, OTP 28.5.0.9, and OTP 29.0.3, corresponding to ssl from 5.3.4 before 11.2.12.10, 11.6.0.8, and 11.7.3.

item.title: CVE-2026-130411 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.2
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.2 | Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in woylie flop allows a remote attacker to execute code on the server via a crafted pagination cursor.
Flop.Cursor.decode/2 in lib/flop/cursor.ex decodes the after and before parameters with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 in :safe mode. Its check rejects functions, PIDs, ports and references, but it accepts maps, and therefore structs of any module. Flop passes the decoded values to Ecto as query parameters. A cursor value that nests an Ecto.Query.DynamicExpr struct with a DBConnection.Stream struct as its binding fails the Ecto cast. Ecto then inspects the value for the error message, the Inspect implementation enumerates the stream, and DBConnection calls the module, function and arguments in the :log option of the stream.
This issue affects flop: from 0.8.0 before 0.26.7, from 0.27.0 before 0.27.3, from 0.28.0 before 0.28.1, and from 0.29.0 before 0.29.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-131902 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9 | XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an object version id passed to ExAws.S3.delete_multiple_objects/3 to add objects to the batch delete.
delete_multiple_objects/3 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the <Delete> request body by placing each object's version between <VersionId> tags without XML escaping. A version such as v1</VersionId></Object><Object><Key>important-file</Key></Object><Object><Key>x</Key><VersionId>v2 closes the caller's object and opens new ones, so S3 deletes objects the application never listed, including other users' objects in the same bucket.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133555 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.9 | Use of Externally-Controlled Input to Select Classes or Code ('Unsafe Reflection') vulnerability in elixir-ecto db_connection allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code via a forged DBConnection.Stream or DBConnection.PrepareStream struct. The Enumerable implementations of both structs in lib/db_connection.ex run with the options stored in the struct. The :log option accepts a {module, function, arguments} tuple, which DBConnection applies. When code enumerates a forged struct, DBConnection calls the chosen function.
This issue is not exploitable in db_connection alone. It is, in theory, a vulnerability of the downstream component. The root cause is a component that decodes untrusted input with :erlang.binary_to_term/2 and does not restrict which terms the result contains. The :safe option does not reject structs, and these structs contain only plain terms. Structs of other libraries can possibly lead to the same result, so a component that decodes untrusted terms stays at risk independently of db_connection. This record exists because the struct was used in attacks on such components.
This issue affects db_connection: from 1.1.0 before 2.10.3.

item.title: CVE-2026-135908 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3

item.title: CVE-2026-136155 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Valkey 9.1.0 and 9.1.1, the Lua script debugger builds its command table once and caches it with a pointer to the Lua interpreter state that was current at the time. SCRIPT FLUSH ASYNC recreates the scripting engine and frees the previous interpreter state without invalidating that cache, so the next debugger command dereferences freed memory. An authenticated user who can run scripting commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and by reclaiming the freed heap chunk with attacker-controlled bytes can escalate it to control of an indirect call, which may lead to remote code execution. The fix also addresses a second use-after-free in ldbLogStackValue. Valkey 8.0.x and 8.1.x use the previous debugger and are not affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-136156 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Valkey before 7.2.15, 8.0.x before 8.0.12, 8.1.x before 8.1.11, 9.0.x before 9.0.7, 9.1.x before 9.1.3 and 9.2.0-rc1, running in cluster mode, clusterCreatePublishMsgBlock computes the length of the cluster bus message for a PUBLISH or SPUBLISH as a size_t but passes it to createClusterMsgSendBlock as a uint32_t. When the channel and message together exceed 4 GiB, the length is truncated, a buffer far smaller than the message is allocated, and the full channel and message are then copied into it. An authenticated user who can publish, for example by building the arguments in a script, can overflow the heap with attacker-controlled bytes. This reliably crashes the server and may lead to remote code execution. Servers that do not run in cluster mode are not affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-136157 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | In Valkey 8.0.x before 8.0.11, 8.1.x before 8.1.10, 9.0.x before 9.0.6 and 9.1.x before 9.1.2, the RDMA transport's pending-data handler walks its connection list with an iterator that caches the next entry. A command processed from inside that loop, such as CLIENT KILL, can synchronously free another client's connection, and closing an RDMA connection did not remove it from the pending list, so the handler then uses freed memory. An authenticated user can use this to reliably crash the server, and the freed heap chunk can be reclaimed with attacker-influenced bytes. Only servers built with RDMA support (USE_RDMA) and configured with an RDMA listener are affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-136158 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | In Valkey JSON 1.0.0 through 1.0.2, a recursive JSONPath expression such as $..* returns both an array and elements nested inside it. The size-changing mutators (JSON.ARRAPPEND, JSON.ARRINSERT, JSON.ARRPOP, JSON.ARRTRIM and JSON.CLEAR) process the ancestor first, which can reallocate its element buffer and free the old storage while the descendant entries in the result set still point into it; the module then writes through those dangling pointers. An authenticated user who can run these commands can use this to reliably crash the server, and it has been developed into remote code execution as the user the server runs as. Servers that do not load the JSON module, including through valkey-bundle, are not affected.

item.title: CVE-2026-62273 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1 | XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls tag keys or values to inject forged tag entries into S3 object and bucket tagging requests.
ExAws.S3.put_object_tagging/4 and ExAws.S3.put_bucket_tagging/2 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex build the <TagSet> request body by interpolating tag keys and values directly into <Key> and <Value> elements via to_string/1, without applying the module's existing escape_xml_string/1 helper (which delete_multiple_objects already uses for object keys). An application that forwards user-supplied data as a tag key or value lets an attacker close the intended element and inject attacker-chosen <Tag> entries. For example, a tag value of blue</Value></Tag><Tag><Key>owner</Key><Value>admin turns one intended tag into two tags on the wire. Because S3 honors tags in access-control conditions (aws:RequestTag, s3:ExistingObjectTag) and cost-allocation reporting, an injected tag can forge an authorization-relevant tag or corrupt the intended tag set.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.2 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-63581 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 6.9 | XML Injection vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 (ExAws.S3 module) allows an attacker to inject arbitrary XML configuration elements into S3 bucket-configuration request bodies via unescaped, caller-supplied values.
This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/s3.ex and program routines ExAws.S3.put_bucket_logging/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_notification/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_replication/2, ExAws.S3.put_bucket_website/2.
The bucket-configuration body builders construct their XML by interpolating caller-supplied values directly into the request body without escaping, and never route them through the module's own escape_xml_string/1 helper. A value containing XML metacharacters (<, >, &, quotes) can close the intended element early and open attacker-chosen elements, which the builder's trailing closing tag then closes, keeping the document single-rooted and well-formed. In a multi-tenant application where tenants configure their own bucket settings, an attacker who can influence one of the interpolated field values (for example the logging target, a notification ARN, a replication destination or Account, or a website redirect HostName) can inject arbitrary configuration nodes into a request the application signs and sends to AWS. The affected builders are reached through the public functions put_bucket_logging/2, put_bucket_notification/2, put_bucket_replication/2, and put_bucket_website/2.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.5.9 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-63582 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.8
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.8 | Externally Controlled Reference to a Resource in Another Sphere vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows an attacker who controls an S3 bucket name to make presigned URLs and presigned POST forms point at a host of their choice.
With virtual_host: true, s3_accelerate: true or bucket_as_host: true, ExAws.S3.presigned_url/5 and ExAws.S3.presigned_post/4 build the URL from the bucket name without checking it. A bucket such as attacker.example/x? turns the URL into https://attacker.example/x?.s3.amazonaws.com..., and the signature is computed for that host. Clients given the URL upload their files to, or download content from, the attacker's host, and every such URL discloses the access key id. With bucket_as_host: true any valid hostname works as the bucket name.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-63583 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.0
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.0 | ExAws.S3.Utils.build_lifecycle_rule/1 in ex_aws_s3 interpolates caller-supplied lifecycle rule fields (the rule id, filter prefix, tag key and value, storage class, and noncurrent-version count) directly into the PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration XML body without escaping XML metacharacters. An application that populates any of these fields from untrusted input (for example a tenant-supplied object tag) lets an attacker break out of the surrounding element and inject arbitrary XML into the request, including an entirely new lifecycle action such as a delete-after-one-day expiration that destroys the bucket's objects. The public entry point ExAws.S3.put_bucket_lifecycle/2 flows directly into this builder.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.3.0 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-63584 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1 | Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection') vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_s3 allows HTTP header injection via an attacker-controlled copy-source key.
ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 in lib/ex_aws/s3.ex builds the x-amz-copy-source request header by interpolating the source bucket and object key directly into "/#{src_bucket}/#{src_object}" with no percent-encoding. The sibling function put_object_copy percent-encodes the bucket and each path segment before assembling the same header, but upload_part_copy skips encoding entirely.
When the source key is derived from untrusted input, reserved characters (spaces, ?, &, =) pass through verbatim and corrupt the copy-source reference, so the copy targets the wrong object or fails. A key containing \r or \n can split or inject additional headers into the outgoing HTTP request, depending on how the configured HTTP backend serializes headers.
Applications that pass a source bucket or object key derived from untrusted input to ExAws.S3.upload_part_copy/8 are affected. Applications that only ever pass trusted, well-formed keys are not affected.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-63585 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 4.8
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 4.8 | ExAws.S3 constructs S3 ACL grant headers (such as x-amz-grant-read and x-amz-grant-full-control) in format_grant_header/1 by interpolating grantee identifiers into a quoted, comma-separated list without escaping. Grantee email and id values are wrapped in double quotes and joined with a comma, but double-quote, comma, and CR/LF characters in the value are not neutralized. An application that passes an attacker-influenced grantee value (for example an email address taken from a "share this object" feature) into an ACL grant option (grant_read, grant_write, grant_read_acp, grant_write_acp, or grant_full_control) lets the attacker close the quoted token and inject an additional grantee, such as the attacker's own canonical id or the predefined AllUsers group URI, into the header. S3 then applies the injected grantee, granting an arbitrary principal the same permission (up to full control or public access) in an unintended ACL grantee-injection and privilege-escalation issue.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-65320 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 9.2
item.description: Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 9.2 | fastcore through 2.2.44 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the fastcore.xtras.untar_dir() archive extraction helper that allows attackers who supply a crafted tar archive to write files outside the intended extraction directory. The internal _unpack() function passes the archive to shutil.unpack_archive() without a tar extraction filter, member path validation, or a containment check, so archive members with absolute paths or ../ traversal sequences are written to arbitrary locations writable by the application process when running on Python versions before 3.14. Applications that extract untrusted archives with untar_dir() can have application files, configuration, or importable code overwritten, which can lead to code execution, data modification, or denial of service.

item.title: CVE-2026-65621 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 2.1 | ex_aws_s3 builds x-amz-meta-* request headers by interpolating user-supplied object metadata directly into header names and values without any validation. In ExAws.S3.Utils.build_meta_headers/1 (lib/ex_aws/s3/utils.ex), each :meta entry is turned into a header as {"x-amz-meta-#{k}", v} with no check for carriage return (CR), line feed (LF), or other illegal header bytes.
Object metadata is routinely derived from end-user input (for example an upload service that lets users attach a comment or label to an object). When such input reaches ExAws.S3.put_object/4 or any other operation accepting the :meta option, a value containing CR/LF is carried unchanged into the outbound header list. If the configured HTTP adapter does not neutralize header values before writing them to the socket, the embedded CRLF starts a new header line, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary headers into (or split) the HTTP request the library sends to the S3 endpoint. This is an HTTP header (CRLF) injection leading to HTTP request splitting. The practical impact depends on the HTTP adapter, and no authentication is required beyond the ability to influence object metadata.
This issue affects ex_aws_s3: from 2.0.0 before 2.6.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-65622 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9
item.description:
Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9 | Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex-aws ex_aws_ses (ExAws.SES module) allows path injection into Amazon SES V2 request URLs.
This vulnerability is associated with program file lib/ex_aws/ses.ex and program routines ExAws.SES.delete_contact_list/1, ExAws.SES.get_contact_list/1, ExAws.SES.update_contact_list/2, ExAws.SES.create_contact/3, ExAws.SES.get_contact/2, ExAws.SES.update_contact/3, ExAws.SES.delete_contact/2 and ExAws.SES.list_contacts/1.
The V2 contact-list and contact functions interpolate the caller-supplied list_name into the request path without URI-encoding it, unlike the email address in the same functions which is passed through ExAws.Request.Url.uri_encode/1. An application that forwards untrusted input as a contact-list name lets an attacker embed /, .. or ? to escape the intended contact-lists/<name> path segment. A value such as x/../suppression/addresses/victim%40example.com makes a delete_contact_list/1 call arrive at the account-wide suppression list. The request is still signed with the application's own AWS credentials and sent to the configured SES host, so the impact is cross-resource request forgery inside the caller's own AWS account, not arbitrary SSRF. Applications that only use hardcoded or strictly validated list names are not affected.
This issue affects ex_aws_ses: from 2.3.0 before 2.5.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-75582 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
